newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian government said to exploit bomb threat. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Austrian government said to exploit bomb threat. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Austrian opposition parties on Wednesday accused Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's government of exploiting a new bomb scare (corrects from "new series of bomb attacks") ahead of elections on Sunday for Vienna state and the European Parliament.
They added that the police still had no clue who was behind the latest bombing campaign.
The interior ministry on Wednesday trumpeted its success in cracking a coded message sent in a bomb threat made by suspected right-wing extremists last week.

"The government uses all this for their own political ends every time before an election," Greens spokesman Stephan Stennach told Reuters. "There's always some big success story but they still have no idea who is behind these attacks."

Interior Minister Caspar Einem said on Tuesday that information from the codes linked the so-called Bajuwarian Liberation Army (BLA) to more than 20 letter bombs since 1993 and an explosion that killed four gypsy men last year.

Letter bombs were sent in the run-up to general elections in October 1994 and December last year. The latest warning came in the middle of the campaigning for Austria's seats in the Strasbourg-based European Union parliament and for the Vienna state legislature.

Einem's announcement mirrored a similar statement by former interior minister Franz Loeschnak, who said days before the 1994 general election that police were hot on the trail of the perpetrators, Stennach added.

The BLA has claimed responsibility for five waves of letter bombs that have hit Austria since December 1993, injuring 11 people. All the victims were immigrants or figures linked to issues involving foreigners. No one has yet been arrested.
The interior ministry said last week police were tailing 10 suspects, but security chief Michael Sika told Reuters there was no proof they were connected with the latest bomb threat.

The extremists' latest letter, which contained racist language, threatened to blow up eight prominent people. Security around Vranitzky, who was one of the targets named, has been visibly tightened since the warning was issued.

The threat prompted two members of Germany's opposition Social Democrats to cancel a visit to Vienna this week, Austria news agency APA said. One of them, Thomas Rother, was injured last year in a blast caused by a letter bomb sent from Austria.

Helene Partik-Pable of the far-right Freedom Party said in all its boasting over breaking the codes, the government had failed to remind Austrians that no one had yet been arrested for the bombing campaign.
The Liberal Forum's Hans-Helmut Moser criticised the interior ministry for bungling the case since 1993 and said police looked incapable of tackling terrorist activities.
